newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end bourse in party spirits.
newsitem.headline: German shares end bourse in party spirits.

text.p: The Frankfurt bourse charged ahead on Friday, breaking out of a narrow trading range of recent days, boosted by a sparkling performance overnight on Wall Street and in U.S. Treasuries.
"The firm dollar, Wall Street and Bunds are all responsible for taking us into the heavens," one dealer said.
The DAX index of 30 top German shares ended up 46.70 points, or 1.66 percent at 2,854.45 after Wall Street surprised global markets with a 127 point surge overnight, its second biggest net gain ever.
"We're having a party all around the world," said a trader.
In late session trading however, a more moderate dollar and Wall Street's more modest gains helped the IBIS DAX close at 2,835.54 points, or up 10.71.
The DAX had ended bourse trade at 2,807.75 points on Thursday after four days of listless trading, gradually slipping lower in a narrow range.
Dealers said the settlement of the DAX December future contract and the expiry of options on its constituent stocks, so-called triple witching, had helped boost the market.

The expiry is called triple witching because market players with expiring futures positions try and square their positions in the cash market on both the index and individual constituent stocks, which can cause price volatility.

Dealers said shares in electronics firm Siemens, which were very heavily traded during the day, ending afterhours trading weaker than the trend at 71.07 marks, were subject to option expiry volatility.
Some dealers said the day's rally meant the 2,900 point level was once again in sight for the DAX index for the year-end, but others were more cautious.

Shares in German speciality chemicals group Henkel KGaA were one of the biggest DAX gainers, after the company said it had received clearance from the German Federal Cartel Office for its pending acquisition of U.S. adhesives maker Loctite Corp.
The stock was also boosted by news out after Thursday's bourse close that the group plans to acquire the remaining 23 percent of consumer products group Hans Schwarzkopf it does not already own.
Henkel preference shares ended up 2.55 marks at 76.55
